newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Child labor under spotlight at Colombia meeting.
newsitem.headline: Child labor under spotlight at Colombia meeting.

text.p: Efforts to end the exploitation of Latin America's working children will be a top issue on Thursday when international officials begin a two-day conference in this Caribbean port city.

A statement from the International Labour Organisation (ILO), co-sponsor of the meeting with the Colombian government, said Labour ministers and senior government officials from 20 countries across Latin America were expected to attend the conference that will focus on ways to eradicate "the most intolerable forms of child labour."

The Geneva-based ILO is considered to be the world's foremost authority on child labour. It estimated in a report that no less than 15 million children -- or one out of every five -- are employed in some forms of exploitative labour in Latin America, roughly half of them 6 to 14 years old.
An ILO source said child prostitution and the rise of sex-based tourism in cities like Cartagena, was among abusive forms of child labour the meeting would focus on.

Sixty percent of child labourers throughout the Americas are involved in agricultural work, and the source said that too would be a major discussion item. A final declaration to be signed at the meeting will call for stepped-up efforts throughout Latin America to end the exploitation of children.
Carol Bellamy, executive director of the United Nations Children's Fund, told Reuters during a visit to the Colombian capital last week that no end to child labour was in sight anytime soon.
"It is a fact of life in the world today," Bellamy said. "There's no simple answer to the issue of exploitative labour."
